svg.title: Seven extension admission tests
svg.desc: X1 kernel, X2 decision boundary, X3 failure reflection, X4 conformance, X5 legitimate controls, X6 finite resources, X7 no hidden new primitive. Admission precedes scoring. Full definitions and formulas follow in the text.
svg.text: Does this extension count? — the seven admission tests
All seven must pass for admission. Determine membership before scoring an implementation; a passing result does not establish membership.
X1 · Kernel preservation
A mapping preserves every decision-material
relation in the failure kernel.
Bridge → hospital-bed capacity can preserve the kernel;
a case with no shared resource cannot preserve S2.
X2 · Decision-boundary preservation
Identify the receiving decision, with the same
structural proposition and decision dependency.
The subject may change; the role of evidence,
scope, authority and time in the decision may not.
X3 · Failure-predicate reflection
If the extension trace fails, its mapped base trace
must exhibit the same structural failure predicate.
Stale-action downtime may qualify for S5;
downtime caused only by hardware failure does not.
X4 · Acceptance-condition preservation
Every material base condition remains applicable.
Conformance must carry through the trace mapping.
Additional conditions may become material; inherited
conditions may not be weakened to claim membership.
X5 · Positive-control preservation
Preserve legitimate activity: authorized changes
and campaigns, genuine findings and rights claims.
This prevents a deny-everything shortcut
from being counted as an effective solution.
X6 · Finite resources and response
Declare finite deadlines, capacity, cost/burden
and fallback, even when scale changes.
Scaling up does not grant unlimited time,
evidence, reviewers or compute.
X7 · No hidden new primitive
A new decision-material relation or operation not representable in the base kernel makes the variant
a case-family extension candidate, not yet admitted. Record the addition; a separate case may be needed.
Admission and implementation results are separate.
Use the kernel, decision boundary, mappings and controls to establish membership before scoring; never infer it from a PASS.
Record the appropriate first-pass status after reviewing the admission conditions
Strong structural extension
In-family design case; not an executed result.
Candidate extension
Mappings, fixture or source/owner definition pending.
Out-of-family neighbour
A kernel relation is absent; not family evidence.
Reading aid for Annex X, Sections 4, 5 and 9. The exact tests and mathematical definitions remain in the accompanying text.
